Glossary

    Ratio, proportion, percent

    Words: 2498

    A part of a whole and a constant product: two laws behind percentages, mixtures, playback speed and discounts. One law, three questions to it and one limit. At this limit four NMT candidates out of five lost a point in 2026: only 20.4 % solved the percentage task correctly.

    Main idea of the page #

    A percentage does not exist on its own. «20 %» is always «20 % of something». Almost all mistakes in percentage tasks come not from not knowing the formula but from a forgotten «of what». There is one formula here, and the whole you count from changes after every step.

    Step 0 · Hook

    1 · The price rose by 20 % and fell by 20 % #

    An item cost 100 UAH. The price was raised by 20 %, and a week later lowered by 20 %. How much does the item cost now?

    The usual answer: «+20 and −20 give zero, so 100 UAH». Let us check step by step:

    • after the rise: 100 + 20 % of 100 = 100 + 20 = 120 UAH;
    • after the fall: 120 − 20 % of 120 = 120 − 24 = 96 UAH.

    The price did not come back: it fell by 4 %. Both times it was «20 %», but of different wholes: first of 100, then of 120. The habit of adding percentages has just given a wrong answer. Below is why.

    Figure 4. Two steps of 20 % of different wholes: 100 → 120 → 96.

    Step 1 · Concept

    2 · What a percentage is #

    A PercentOne hundredth part; a percentage is always taken of some whole.To the glossary is one hundredth part: 1%=11001\% = \frac{1}{100}. So p%=p100p\% = \frac{p}{100}, and any percentage is simply a fraction written in another language:

    25%=25100=0.25=1425\% = \frac{25}{100} = 0.25 = \frac{1}{4}

    Here are three words to tell apart:

    • Whole, part, shareThe whole is what you count from, the part is what was taken, the share is what fraction the part makes up.To the glossary - the quantity you count from (the price before the change, the whole mass of the solution, the whole distance);
    • the part - what was taken from the whole;
    • the share - the number that shows what fraction of the whole the part makes up. A share is written as a fraction, a decimal or a percentage - it is one and the same number.
    Step 2 · Law

    3 · Part = whole × share #

    Law of the part

    A=B·p100A = B \cdot \frac{p}{100}

    BB is the whole, AA is the part, pp is what percentage of the whole the part makes up.

    Corollary of the law «Law of the part»

    A chart is read with the law of the part

    αsector=360∘·p100\alpha_{\text{sector}} = 360^\circ \cdot \frac{p}{100}

    A bar chart shows amounts, and the whole is their sum. A pie chart shows shares: a sector of p % takes 360° · p/100. A chart of changes shows deviations from a base: new value = base + deviation.

    Why it is so. A chart is the same law of the part, drawn: the whole is the sum of all the bars or the whole circle, 360°, the part is one bar or one sector. So first find out what the whole is on the chart and in what units the axis is labelled, and then calculate as in any task on the part.

    The formula has three participants, and you can ask about any of them. These are not three different tasks but one law read in three ways:

    • find the part: A=B·p100A = B \cdot \frac{p}{100};
    • find the whole: B=A:p100B = A : \frac{p}{100};
    • find the percentage: p=AB·100p = \frac{A}{B} \cdot 100.

    A second law follows from it, about changing a quantity by a percentage:

    Law of change

    Bnew=B·(1+p100)B_{\text{new}} = B \cdot \left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)

    For a decrease pp is taken with a minus sign. Several changes in a row multiply, they do not add:

    B·(1+p100)·(1+q100)B \cdot \left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right) \cdot \left(1 + \frac{q}{100}\right)

    And two laws of proportionality from which percentages grew:

    Basic property of a proportion

    ab=cd⟺ad=bc(b,d≠0)\frac{a}{b} = \frac{c}{d} \iff ad = bc \quad (b, d \neq 0)

    Inverse proportion: the product is constant

    v·t=S=const⟹t=Svv \cdot t = S = \text{const} \implies t = \frac{S}{v}

    If one quantity is increased k times, the other decreases k times. Speed and time, the number of workers and the length of the job, the price and the amount of goods for a fixed sum.

    Step 3 · Why it is so

    4 · Where the formula comes from #

    «p percent of B» means: divide B into 100 equal parts and take p of them. One part is B100\frac{B}{100}, p parts are B100·p\frac{B}{100} \cdot p. There is nothing more in the law of the part.

    The law of change is the law of the part together with the distributive law of block 1. The new value is the old one plus its part:

    B+B·p100=B·(1+p100)B + B \cdot \frac{p}{100} = B \cdot \left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)

    A ProportionAn equality of two ratios; its basic property is ad = bc.To the glossary is an equality of two ratios; multiply both sides by bdbd and you get ad=bcad = bc. Inverse proportionA dependence in which the product of two quantities is constant.To the glossary : if v·tv \cdot t is constant, then increasing v k times can be balanced only by decreasing t k times, otherwise the product changes.

    Figure 5. Inverse proportion: the product v · t is constant, like the area of a rectangle.

    The second change is applied to the new value, that is, to the new whole. So the multiplier of the second change multiplies the result of the first. In the hook: 100·1.2·0.8=96100 \cdot 1.2 \cdot 0.8 = 96. The product 1.2·0.8=0.961.2 \cdot 0.8 = 0.96 is exactly those minus 4 %.

    Step 4 · Limits

    5 · Where the law breaks if you forget the whole #

    The whole is what you compare with. «By how many percent is 50 greater than 40?» - you compare with 40: the difference 10 is 25 % of 40. «By how many percent is 40 less than 50?» - you compare with 50: the same difference 10 is only 20 % of 50. One difference, two wholes, two answers.

    Successive percentages do not add. You can add only percentages of one and the same whole. After the first change the whole is different.

    «3 times as much» is «200 % more», not 300 %. The new value is 3B=B·(1+2)3B = B \cdot (1 + 2): the increase is two wholes, that is, 200 %.

    A decrease of more than 100 % is impossible for a price, a mass or a length: the multiplier 1−p1001 - \frac{p}{100} would become negative. You can increase by as many percent as you like.

    Step 5 · Practice

    6 · Tasks in the NMT format #

    Each task here knows its law. If the answer is wrong, the task leads to the law and its limits, not to «the right answer».

    One answer out of five · 1 point

    Find three eighths of the number 320.

    Law: part = whole × share.

    The share is 38\frac{3}{8}. The wrong options are blind moves: 40 - only one eighth was found, 200 - the remainder was found, 280 - one eighth was subtracted, 960 - multiplied by 3 and forgot to divide.

    Short answer · 2 points

    A tariff of 250 UAH was first raised by 12 % and then by another 10 %. How many hryvnias is the new tariff?

    Law: law of change.

    Two changes multiply: 250·1.12·1.1=308250 \cdot 1.12 \cdot 1.1 = 308. The blind move «12 + 10 = 22 %» gives 305: the difference of three hryvnias is that very limit.

    Short answer · 2 points

    A video lesson lasts 36 minutes. Before watching, the playback speed was increased 1.5 times. How many minutes will the viewing take?

    Law: inverse proportion.

    The length of the clip is constant, so time = length : speed, t=361.5=24t = \frac{36}{1.5} = 24. The limit: if the factor is less than 1, the viewing becomes longer. And one more check of the law of the part: the speed grew by 50 %, while the time fell by 12 minutes out of 36, that is, by 3313%33\frac{1}{3}\%, not by 50 %.

    Matching · 3 points

    The numbers 80 and 100. Match each question (1-3) with its answer (A-E).

    A · 20 %   B · 25 %   C · 80 %   D · 120 %   E · 125 %

    Law: find the percentage.

    The percentage: p=AB·100p = \frac{A}{B} \cdot 100. Three questions, one pair of numbers, but the whole is different each time: in the first and the third it is 100, in the second 80.

    One answer out of five · 1 point

    40 pupils named their favourite game: 10 football, 14 basketball, 16 volleyball. What will the angle of the «basketball» sector be on a pie chart of these data?

    Figure 6. For the task: a pie chart in which a sector is a share of the whole.

    Corollary: a chart is read with the law of the part.

    A sector is the same share of 360° as the part is of the whole: 1440·360∘=126∘\frac{14}{40} \cdot 360^\circ = 126^\circ. 90° is the football sector, 144° the volleyball one.

    Short answer · 2 points

    Data on the figure · read and apply. The numbers for the solution are only on the figure: first write them down, then solve.

    Using the chart, find what percentage of all the books sold over the five days was sold on Wednesday and Thursday together.

    Figure 7. For the task: book sales over five days.

    Law: part = whole × share.

    From the chart: 12, 18, 30, 24, 6, in all 90. Wednesday and Thursday: 30 + 24 = 54. The share is 54 : 90 = 0.6, that is, 60%.

    One answer out of five · 1 point

    Data on the figure · pick what is needed. The numbers are only on the figure, and among them is an extra one or a trap: the grid step, a scale that does not start at zero. Write down only what the solution needs.

    Using the chart, find how many times as many visitors there were on Saturday as on Tuesday.

    Figure 8. For the task: a chart whose scale does not start at zero.

    Corollary: a chart is read with the law of the part.

    The scale starts at 40, so the heights of the bars are not proportional to the numbers. Read the numbers: Saturday 80, Tuesday 50. 80 : 50 = 1.6. The answer 4 is the ratio of the bar heights, not of the numbers.

    Short answer · 2 points

    Data on the figure · read and connect. The numbers are only on the figure, and what you read goes into two laws: write the numbers down, then name both laws.

    Using the chart, find by how many percent the price in March is higher than in January.

    Figure 9. For the task: the price of apples over four months.

    Laws: the law of change and part = whole × share.

    From the chart: January 40 UAH, March 50 UAH. The change 50 − 40 = 10 UAH is counted from January, which is what you compare with: 10 : 40 = 0.25, that is, 25%. Whoever divides by 50 gets 20%.
    Step 6 · Reverse move

    7 · Name the law yourself #

    Here the law is not given. First tell yourself which law works and from which whole to count, and only then calculate. The solution opens after you answer.

    Short answer · 2 points

    A price was lowered by 25 % and then raised by 25 %. By how many percent is the new price lower than the original one?

    Law: law of change.

    0.75·1.25=0.93750.75 \cdot 1.25 = 0.9375, so the price is lower by 6.25 %. The hook from the top of the page, but with other numbers.

    Short answer · 2 points

    A solution contains 18 g of salt, and that is 6 % of the mass of the solution. What is the mass of the solution in grams?

    Law: the law of the part, read for the whole.

    B=18:0.06=300B = 18 : 0.06 = 300. The story about salt adds nothing to the mathematics: it is the same «find the whole».

    Short answer · 2 points

    A cyclist covers the distance between two villages in 2 hours. In how many minutes will he cover this distance if he increases his speed by 25 %?

    Laws: the law of change and inverse proportion.

    The new speed is 1.251.25 of the old one. Inverse proportion: the time is divided by the same factor, 120:1.25=96120 : 1.25 = 96 minutes. The blind move «the time is also 25 % less» gives 90 minutes.

    8 · Find the mistake in someone else's solution #

    Olenka reasons: «The item became 20 % cheaper. To get back to the previous price, it must become 20 % dearer».

    Where is the mistake?

    The second change is counted from the new, lower price. The price became 0.8B0.8B, and to get back BB it must be multiplied by 10.8=1.25\frac{1}{0.8} = 1.25, that is, raised by 25 %. Olenka forgot that the whole had changed. This is the second limit of the law.

    What you have after this page #

    One law instead of ten kinds of tasks. Find the part, find the whole, find the percentage, raise, lower, compare: it is one law of the part and the question «of what».

    Frequency on this site, not in the NMT: this page has 11 trainer tasks, and they lean on these laws: Law of the part - 7, Law of change - 4, Inverse proportion: the product is constant - 2. In real NMT papers of 2024-2026 this block is needed in 12 tasks out of 132: Law of the part - 7, Basic property of a proportion - 3, Law of change - 2, Inverse proportion: the product is constant - 1.

    Check yourself with three questions. You know this law if you:

    1. solve 8 percentage tasks out of 10 without a hint;
    2. can explain aloud why two changes of 20 % do not bring the price back;
    3. find the mistake in someone else's solution, as in Olenka's.
